title: Canada Now Counts Stipend-Paid Work for Professors Seeking Express Entry
excerpt: A temporary public policy effective November 17 lets university professors and lecturers paid through stipends, grants, bursaries or scholarships count that Canadian work toward permanent residence — while teaching and research assistants lose category eligibility.
body:
• Canada now recognises stipends, grants, bursaries and scholarships as pay for university professors and lecturers (NOC 41200) under Express Entry, under a temporary public policy that took effect on November 17, 2026.
  • Qualifying Canadian experience can count toward the Canadian Experience Class and Federal Skilled Worker Program, and toward Comprehensive Ranking System points — 70 points for a year of qualifying experience, or 100 for a qualifying job offer.
  • If this describes you, IRCC's advice is direct: update your Express Entry profile to reflect the experience. Only candidates invited to apply on or after November 17 are covered.
  • Post-secondary teaching and research assistants (NOC 41201) were removed from the researchers category on the same day, leaving professors and lecturers as its sole eligible occupation.

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) has begun recognising non-wage pay for university professors and lecturers under Express Entry, in a change that took effect by way of a temporary public policy on November 17, 2026. Professors and lecturers (National Occupational Classification 41200) paid by a Canadian entity through stipends, grants, bursaries or scholarships may now count that work both as qualifying experience and toward job offers under Express Entry, IRCC said in a notice published on November 18.

Who is affected — and who is not

The change affects foreign nationals working in Canada as university professors and lecturers whose pay comes in the forms common in academia — a research stipend, a grant, a bursary or a scholarship — rather than as wages. It does not affect academics already paid a salary, whose experience already counted. And it cuts the other way for a neighbouring group: IRCC has removed post-secondary teaching and research assistants (NOC 41201) from the eligible occupations under the "researchers with Canadian work experience" category, effective November 17, leaving university professors and lecturers as the category's sole eligible occupation, according to CIC News.

What changed, precisely

The mechanism matters here. Under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, "work" for Express Entry purposes is defined as an activity for which wages are paid or commission is earned. That definition excluded the pay structures universities routinely use for researchers, so experience earned on a stipend could not previously count toward the Canadian Experience Class (CEC) or the Federal Skilled Worker Program (FSWP) — the two programs through which most skilled candidates qualify.

The temporary public policy, signed by Immigration Minister Lena Metlege Diab on November 17 under section 25.2 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, exempts qualifying candidates from those standard work-experience requirements. IRCC said recognising non-wage pay "better reflects how many researchers and academics are compensated for their work." The researchers category itself was announced in February 2026, and the policy sits alongside the Global Impact+ Research Talent Initiative, under which Budget 2025 committed $1.7 billion over 12 years to attract more than 1,000 researchers to Canada.

On the numbers: because NOC 41200 sits in the highest tier of IRCC's high-wage occupations list, eligible candidates may receive 70 additional Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) points for at least one year of qualifying Canadian work experience, or 100 points for a qualifying job offer, CIC News reported. Counted here: work experience and job offers in NOC 41200 with a Canadian entity. Not counted: experience in other occupations, or the teaching and research assistant work that has just been removed from the category.

What to do next

IRCC advised candidates with qualifying Canadian experience to update their Express Entry profiles to reflect it — a profile that does not show the experience cannot be selected on the basis of it. The timing condition is strict: the policy covers candidates who receive an invitation to apply through Express Entry on or after November 17, 2026, and then apply under the CEC or FSWP. Those who received an invitation before November 17 are not covered, even if they submit their permanent residence application after that date. Candidates must still meet every other requirement, including language proficiency and admissibility, and the separate pressure on Canada's system remains considerable — IRCC's overall application backlog recently fell to 1.51 million files.

The policy has no predetermined end date, but it can be revoked by the immigration minister at any time — a reason for eligible professors and lecturers to update their profiles now rather than assume the window stays open.
